stage_messages.introduction: Hey Doctor! Eleanor needs your help. Start with what happened, then keep your patient safe. You’ve got this!
stage_messages.history: Good questions uncover the mechanism and red flags. You do not need to ask everything—ask what changes your decisions.
stage_messages.examination: Slow and safe. Inspect first, localize tenderness and protect injured structures while checking nerves and circulation.
stage_messages.investigations: Choose the smallest clinically sufficient set of tests. I’ll show you each written report as you order it.
stage_messages.diagnosis: Now connect the mechanism, examination and investigations. Which diagnosis actually explains all three?
stage_messages.treatment: The treatment tray is shuffled. Each safe action gets its sequence number when its prerequisites are complete.
stage_messages.knowledge_check: Nice work! Three quick questions to lock in the clinical reasoning.
stage_messages.completion: Great job with Eleanor! The best clinicians are careful about both decisions and patient safety.

case_specific_guidance.differentiating_clue: There is an impacted surgical-neck line with minimal displacement and no dislocation.
case_specific_guidance.clinical_coaching: Minimally displaced proximal humerus surgical-neck fracture: pain control, sling, distal joint motion, staged early shoulder rehabilitation and follow-up.
key_teaching_points: Minimal displacement usually favors nonoperative care.
Axillary nerve and joint alignment must be assessed.
Begin graded motion as pain/stability allow, avoiding prolonged unnecessary immobilization.
Older adult low-energy fractures are an opportunity to evaluate bone health.

history.message: Focus on the injury mechanism, neurovascular symptoms, wounds and other associated injuries. Low-energy direct impact to shoulder with no seizure or dislocation mechanism.

examination.message: Start with these case-specific findings: Axillary sensory patch intact. Radial/median/ulnar function intact. Red flag: New neurovascular deficit.

investigations.message: Select investigations that will change management. Initial priority: Left shoulder AP and scapular-Y radiographs. Is the humeral head still aligned with the glenoid?
